picked.t: 베트남 빈스피드, 獨지멘스와 ‘고속철’ 계약 체결…10억 유로 규모
picked.body: 빈스피드의 고속열차 예상 이미지. (이미지=빈그룹) 베트남 고속철도 전문 업체 빈스피드(VinSpeed)가 독일 지멘스모빌리티(Siemens Mobility)와 10억 유로(약 11억3,920만 달러) 규모의 고속철도 기관차 공급계약을 체결했다. 로이터통신에 따르면, 이번 계약은 지난해 양사가 체결한 기본 협약을 구체화한 것으로, 해당 파트너십은 빈스피드의 하노이-하롱 구간과 호치민시 벤탄-껀저 고속철도 철로 건설과 고속철도 운행을 주요 내용으로 한다. 빈스피드의 최대 주주인 빈그룹(Vingroup)은 해당 보도와 계약 규모를 확인했다. 앞서 양사가 지난해 체결한 기본 협약에는 지멘스 측의 △신호 △통신 △전력공급 등 핵심 시스템 △빈스피드 프로젝트용 열차 및 시스템 공급·통합 등이 포함된다. 지멘스는 기술 이전을 조율하고 운행 중 유지보수 방안도 함께 연구할 예정이다. 지멘스모빌리티는 미국·러시아·중국 등지의 최첨단 고속철도 시스템 구축의 토대를 마련한 업력 175여 년의 독일 지멘스의 철도·운송 기술 공급업체다. 빈스피드는 팜 녓 브엉(Pham Nhat Vuong) 빈그룹 회장이 지난해 5월 설립한 고속철도 전문업체로, 현재 주주 구성은 브엉 회장이 지분 51%를 보유한 최대 주주에 올라있으며, 베트남투자그룹(Vietnam Investment Group) 35%, 빈그룹 10% 브엉 회장의 장·차남인 팜 녓 꾸언 안(Pham Nhat Quan Anh)과 팜 녓 민 황(Pham Nhat Minh Hoang)이 각 1%를 보유하고 있다. 빈스피드의 자본금은 약 45조 동(약 17억3,240만 달러)으로, 철도 건설과 철도차량 제조 사업을 영위하고 있다. 현재 빈스피드가 추진 중인 총연장 54km 벤탄-껀저 고속철도와 120km 하노이-하롱 고속철도의 총사업비는 202조 동(77억7,640만여 달러)으로 오는 2028년 상업 운행을 목표로 한다.

picked.t: 다낭서 한국인 연루 ‘불법 환치기’ 조직 적발…38.5만 달러 규모
picked.body: 다낭에서 불법 국경 간 외화 이체 혐의로 붙잡힌 40대 베트남인 T씨의 모습. (사진=호치민시공안신문) 베트남 다낭에서 한국인 2명이 연루된 불법 환치기 조직이 현지 공안 당국에 적발됐다. 베트남 매체 뚜오이쩨(Tuoitre)는 지역 매체를 인용해 “한국인 2명이 연루된 불법 국경 간 외화 이체 조직이 공안 당국에 적발됐다’고 지난 25일 보도했다. 이들은 올해 초부터 100억 동(약 38.5만 달러) 이상을 이체한 혐의를 받는다. 당국에 따르면, 베트남 이민 당국은 외국인 체류·관리 단속의 일환으로 지난 7월 8일 응우한선(Ngu Hanh Son) 지역 부몽응우옌길(Vu Mong Nguyen) 소재 한 주택을 단속하다 입국 목적을 위반한 것으로 의심되는 한국인 2명을 적발했다. 이후 수사관들은 50대 한국인 M씨가 한국과 베트남 간 송금·환전에 연루된 사실을 확인했다. M씨는 한국에서 베트남으로 직접 송금하는 대신 다수의 중개 계좌를 활용한 것으로 드러났다. 구체적으로 M씨는 한국 원화를 한국 내 베트남인 명의 계좌에 입금한 뒤, 이에 상응하는 베트남 동화는 다낭 현지 연락책인 40대 베트남인 T씨가 수령해 시내에서 M씨에게 건네는 방식이었다. 거래는 소액으로 쪼개져 양국의 여러 계좌를 통해 이뤄졌으며, 계좌이체와 현금전달을 병행하는 방식이었다. 조직은 카카오톡을 통해 송금 지시와 영수증 이미지를 주고받으며 내역을 확인했다. 당국에 따르면, T씨는 지난 5월 한 달간 2,425만 원 상당 송금·환전에 관여한 것으로 드러났으며, 올해 초부터 이들이 처리한 거래액은 38만5,000달러에 이르는 것으로 파악됐다. 다낭시 공안 경제범죄수사국은 지난 24일 T씨를 불법 국경간 외화 이체 혐의로 입건하고, 수사 기간 출국을 금지했다. 당국은 전체 자금 흐름을 추적하고 다른 연루자를 특정하기 위해 수사를 확대하고 있다.

picked.t: 하이랜드커피 창업주, 졸리비 베트남법인 지분 11% 인수에 ‘경영권’ 확보…8,800만 달러 규모
picked.body: 베트남 호치민시의 한 하이랜드커피 매장. 베트남 대표 커피 체인 하이랜드커피(Highlands Coffee)의 창업주가 동사 경영권 확보를 위해 필리핀 졸리비푸드(Jollibee Foods Corporation, JFC)로부터 지분 11%를 매입할 계획이다. 거래가 완료되면, 데이비드 타이(David Thai) 대표가 이끄는 비엣타이인터내셔널(Viet Thai International, VTI)의 지분율은 51%로 확대돼 하이랜드커피의 경영권을 확보하게 된다. 졸리비푸드는 최근 완전 자회사인 JSF인베스트먼트(JSF Investments Pte. Ltd.)가 SF붕따우(SF Vung Tau JSC)의 주식 약 150만 주를 VTI에 매각하는 내용의 계약을 체결했다고 밝혔다. SF붕따우는 베트남 내 하이랜드커피 사업을 운영하는 법인이며, VTI는 지난 1998년 하이랜드커피 창업자이자 현재 대표인 데이비드 타이 CEO가 설립한 회사다. 이번 거래 규모는 조정분을 제외하고 8,800만 달러로, 이를 기준으로 한 하이랜드커피 지분 가치는 8억 달러로 추산된다. 거래가 완료되면 SF붕따우에 대한 졸리비푸드의 지분은 60%에서 49%로 줄고, VTI 지분은 40%에서 51%로 늘어 최대 주주로서 경영권을 확보하게 된다. 이번 거래는 필요한 규제 당국과 주주 승인 등 일부 완료 조건을 남겨두고 있다. 이에 대해 졸리비푸드는 경영권을 넘긴 이후에도 49%의 지분을 계속 보유해 향후 브랜드 성장에 따른 이익을 지속적으로 누릴 수 있다고 밝혔다. 동사는 이번 지분 매각대금 약 8,800만 달러를 부채 상환과 다른 성장 사업에 대한 재투자, 주주 환원 등에 사용할 예정이다. 이번 거래는 졸리비푸드가 지난 2012년 하이랜드커피에 대한 첫 투자에 나선 뒤 브랜드가 크게 성장한 시점에서 이뤄졌다. 졸리비푸드의 투자 당시 하이랜드커피의 전국 매장 수는 56곳에 불과했으나, 작년말 기준 매장 수는 베트남 947곳, 필리핀 38곳을 포함 총 985개까지 크게 확대됐다. 이어 6월 말 기준 하이랜드커피의 매장 수는 1,000개에 도달했다. 한편, 지난 2분기 기준 하이랜드커피 매출은 전년 동기 대비 46.7% 증가했고, 베트남 수익성 개선의 핵심 지표인 최소 15개월 이상 운영된 동일매장매출(Same-store sales)은 11.5% 증가했다. 특히 EBITDA(법인세·이자·감가상각비 차감전 영업이익)는 10억 페소를 넘어섰다. 이는 전년 동기 대비 70% 이상 증가한 것으로, 별도 실적 공시가 시작된 2023년 3분기 이후 분기 최고치에 해당한다. 상반기 기준 누적 EBITDA는 17억 페소를 넘어서며 전년 동기 대비 39%의 성장세를 보였다. 현재 하이랜드커피의 이용객은 연간 1억 명 이상을 기록하고 있다. VTI로의 경영권 이전은 하이랜드커피가 베트남 내 기업공개(IPO) 및 상장을 준비하는 시점에 이뤄졌다. 앞서 졸리비푸드는 지난 3월 하이랜드커피 이사회가 베트남 내 독립적인 IPO를 검토하고 있으며, 목표 시점은 2027년 1분기라고 밝힌 바 있다. 하이랜드커피의 상장이 현실화되면, 자본 시장에 대한 직접 접근으로, 다음 성장 단계를 위한 재원이 확보될 것으로 기대를 모은다. 앞서 블룸버그는는 소식통을 인용해 하이랜즈커피가 베트남 IPO를 통해 약 3억~4억 달러를 조달할 수 있다고 보도한 바 있다. 하이랜드커피는 지난 1999년 타이 대표가 설립한 커피 브랜드로, 2012년 졸리비푸드는 2,500만 달러를 투자해 베트남 사업 지분 49%와 홍콩 사업 지분 60%를 인수한 바 있다. 타이 대표는 졸리비푸드의 지배 지분 인수 이후에도 하이랜드커피가 여전히 베트남 커피 브랜드라는 점을 강조해오고 있다.

picked.t: In Da Nang's Tam Tien, sunrise brings fish market to life
picked.body: Twenty years ago, Tam Tien Fish Market in Da Nang City was just a landing spot for fishing boats. Today, after the number of boats grew, traders began gathering there, turning it into a market. Visitors who arrive in the early morning can now see hundreds of fishing boats pull ashore at once. Khanh Phan, who lives in Ho Chi Minh City, has returned to Tam Tien Fish Market many times to capture its colors. To photograph the boats against the sun, she waits for the sun to rise red over the sea and uses a telephoto lens. Located on the coast of Ha Loc Village in Tam Xuan Commune, this summer-only market offers fresh seafood and a glimpse into local life. Photographers also frequent the market to document the lives of fishermen. "I keep coming back here year after year," Khanh says. Her last visit was in early July. Khanh usually photographs the market in two shifts: from 4:30 a.m. to 6 a.m., when returning boats make it busiest, and from 6 a.m. to 7 a.m., when trading and the morning light make for the best photos. For wide market shots, Khanh suggests arriving at around 5:15 a.m. when the sun rises. Using a wide-angle lens lets you capture the market in the foreground, boats on the water in the middle, and the sky overhead. Using a drone to capture waves crashing onto the shore is another method she enjoys. As the boats approach the shore, fishermen transfer their catch into basket boats to take ashore. Traders waiting on the beach rush to meet each basket and pick out what they want. Catches such as swordfish, grouper, and squid are then laid out for selling along the beach, drawing both locals and tourists. picked.t: Hong Ngoc Hospital offers maternity care for international families in Hanoi
picked.body: The hospital offers maternity care covering antenatal examinations, prenatal screening, childbirth and postpartum follow-up, allowing expectant mothers to receive care within the same hospital system throughout pregnancy. The approach helps maintain consistent medical records and reduces the need to move between healthcare facilities at different stages of care. The hospital is accredited by the Australian Council on Healthcare Standards International (ACHSI) and recognized by the Royal College of Surgeons of England (RCS) as an international-standard surgical education center. Its quality management procedures cover medical examinations, infection prevention and control, medication management, surgery and patient safety. In maternal and newborn care, Hong Ngoc is the first private hospital in northern Vietnam recognized as a Center of Excellence for Breastfeeding Practices. It also operates a satellite human milk bank under the Human Milk Bank at Vietnam National Children's Hospital. The milk bank provides pasteurized donor human milk to newborns when medically indicated, while mothers receive breastfeeding guidance after childbirth. The Obstetrics and Gynecology Department includes physicians with doctoral and master's degrees and Specialist Level I and II qualifications. Many have previously worked at institutions including the National Hospital of Obstetrics and Gynecology and Hanoi Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital. The team provides routine antenatal care, high-risk pregnancy management, vaginal delivery, cesarean sections, and diagnosis and treatment of gynecological conditions. For international families, language assistance is available throughout the care process. Some physicians communicate directly with patients in English, while additional support is available in Korean, Japanese and Chinese. The multilingual service covers appointments, administrative procedures, examinations and treatment, helping patients understand test results, medical instructions, delivery options and potential complications. International patients can book appointments through the hospital's hotline or mobile application and receive reminders for pregnancy checkups. Medical examinations are available on weekends and selected public holidays, while emergency services, laboratory testing and diagnostic imaging operate around the clock. For patients continuing treatment overseas, the hospital assists with preparing and transferring medical records and coordinating with receiving healthcare facilities. Hong Ngoc works with more than 50 domestic and international insurance providers. Staff help patients check benefits, prepare documents and arrange direct billing where permitted by their policies. The hospital offers single, double and VIP inpatient rooms for mothers and accompanying family members. Rooms include internet access and essential amenities, while meals are tailored to patients' medical conditions and nutritional needs. Nursing staff are available 24/7. Maternity care packages cover different stages of pregnancy and include antenatal examinations, ultrasound scans, prenatal screening and nutritional counseling. Delivery plans are determined by each patient's clinical condition and medical indications. Mothers and newborns receive care through delivery rooms, operating theaters and recovery units, with postpartum assistance and breastfeeding guidance. For high-risk pregnancies involving diabetes, hypertension, preeclampsia, placenta previa, multiple pregnancies or fetal growth restriction, physicians develop individualized monitoring plans and coordinate care across specialties when needed. The Gynecology and Breast Unit provides examinations and treatment for gynecological conditions, breast examinations and cancer screening. Minimally invasive procedures are available when clinically appropriate and may reduce hospital stays and recovery time. Obstetrics and gynecology services are available at Yen Ninh and Phuc Truong Minh facilities in Hanoi. Both provide pregnancy, childbirth and women's health care, supported by multilingual services and coordination among specialties.

Around 412,000 Vietnamese went abroad for work between 2022 and 2025, according to a report released by the General Statistics Office of Vietnam. Median refers to the middle value in a list. The rate of unmarried guest workers increased from 52% in 2021 to 61% in 2025. The report was based on the 2025 Labor Force Survey and an in-depth survey of guest workers. The geographic origins of people going overseas have also shifted. Five years ago, 83% were from the north central region, including Thanh Hoa, Nghe An, Ha Tinh, Quang Tri and Hue, and the Red River Delta, including Hai Phong, Hung Yen, Bac Ninh, Ninh Binh, and Hanoi. By 2025, the share of the northern midlands and mountainous regions, including Phu Tho, Tuyen Quang, and Thai Nguyen, and the Mekong Delta, including Can Tho and Vinh Long, had risen from 12% to 23%. About 80% of those working abroad had completed high school, but most were in jobs requiring low or medium skills. Manufacturing accounted for 45% of the total jobs, with the other major sectors including construction, agriculture, trade, automobile and motorcycle repair, and accommodation and food services. Incomes varied considerably by occupation. Managers and high- and mid-level technical professionals earned VND51.7 million ($1,960) a month, nearly twice the overall average of VND28 million ($1,077). Workers in simple manual tasks earned more than VND24 million ($923), while skilled trades and agricultural workers and craft workers generally got VND27-29 million. The General Statistics Office said the income gap shows that vocational training, technical skills, and foreign language skills are important for workers seeking higher-paying jobs. It recommended tailoring training programs to the needs of each market. Vietnamese workers were employed in 42 countries and territories, but with nearly 77% in Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan. The General Statistics Office recommended expanding to markets with steady labor demand, good working conditions, and higher salaries, giving workers more options and reducing possible risks from policy changes.

picked.t: Nam A Bank secures $60M from FMO for green finance, small businesses
picked.body: The signing ceremony on Sept. 25 was attended by Hanna Pors, Deputy Consul General of the Netherlands in Ho Chi Minh City, along with senior representatives of Nam A Bank and FMO. The agreement further reinforces Nam A Bank's reputation, international- standard governance capabilities and commitment to sustainable development. Under the agreement, Nam A Bank will prioritize green projects while expanding lending to micro enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The five-year loan will support agriculture, agricultural value chains and rural development, as well as farmers and businesses owned or led by women and young people. The financing is also intended to improve access to longer-term funding for businesses facing financing constraints and support companies seeking to reduce emissions, respond to climate change and adopt more sustainable production models. Vo Hoang Hai, Deputy CEO of Nam A Bank, said the financing would allow the bank to expand green lending and the social impact of its credit activities. "The financing from FMO will be directed toward customer groups that still have considerable unmet financing needs, allowing the bank to expand its social impact alongside its green growth objectives," Hai said. "It is also the result of years of building credibility and reflects Nam A Bank's strategy of diversifying its international funding sources." Frouke Hoekstra, Director of Financial Institutions at FMO, said the partnership supports two of the development bank's priorities: the green transition and access to finance for underserved businesses. "By providing long-term financing for green projects, micro enterprises and SMEs, including women- and youth-owned businesses, we aim to support a more sustainable and inclusive private sector in Vietnam," she said. Hanna Pors, Deputy Consul General of the Netherlands in Ho Chi Minh City, said Vietnam-Netherlands cooperation is increasingly moving from experience sharing toward developing long-term solutions for sustainable development, with green finance playing a growing role. She said the agreement could help translate international capital, expertise and networks into development opportunities in Vietnam, while supporting Nam A Bank's efforts to strengthen ties with international financial institutions. The agreement follows an ESG forum held in Hanoi on Sept. 22 by the Embassy of the Netherlands in Vietnam and FMO. The "ESG Insights for Banking Leaders" event brought together senior executives from FMO's partner banks to discuss integrating environmental, social and governance (ESG) risk management into board-level decisions. The FMO financing follows another international credit agreement signed by Nam A Bank earlier this month. On Sept. 9, the bank secured a $30 million credit facility from French development finance institution Proparco for green finance, bringing its international financing signed in September to $90 million. Nam A Bank has been expanding its green credit portfolio and integrating an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) into its lending operations. The bank said international financing has supported longer-term funding for renewable energy, high-tech agriculture and SMEs. FMO is the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank, investing in private-sector projects in developing and emerging markets. It focuses on areas including agribusiness, food and forestry, energy and financial institutions. FMO has more than 55 years of experience and a committed portfolio of approximately €16 billion across more than 85 countries.

picked.t: Ho Chi Minh City warns of severe flooding as high tides peak at 1.85 m
picked.body: Heavy rain combined with rising tides during the afternoon and evening could cause severe flooding in low-lying areas and along rivers and canals across the city. The Southern Regional Hydro-Meteorological Center announced on Sept. 27 that water levels at most monitoring stations will continue to rise over the next few days before gradually receding. The current high-tide cycle will peak daily between 6 a.m. and 8 a.m., and again from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m., through Sept. 30. At the Phu An Station in the city's central area and the Nha Be Station near the southern Phu My Hung residential area, peak water levels could reach 1.6 to 1.65 m, slightly surpassing the Level 3 alert threshold. At the Thu Dau Mot Station in the former Binh Duong Province, the peak could reach 1.75 to 1.85 m, exceeding the Level 3 alert by up to 0.25 m. The weather agency warned that the combined impact of heavy downpours and tidal surges will directly disrupt traffic and daily life. Residents are advised to prepare for possible deep flooding, limit travel through flood-prone areas, and closely monitor weather forecasts to respond promptly.

picked.t: Vietnam banh mi festival held for first time in Japan
picked.body: The two-day event is the first festival in Japan to feature Vietnamese banh mi as its main theme. Addressing the opening ceremony, Minister-Counselor of the Vietnamese Embassy in Japan Nguyen Sau said banh mi and coffee are two familiar and distinctive Vietnamese specialties that are increasingly popular in Japan and around the world. He said visitors to the festival could not only enjoy Vietnamese food and drinks but also experience a part of the country's culture, people and identity. The diplomat noted that this year's festival coincides with the Mid-Autumn Festival, providing an opportunity for Vietnamese and Japanese families to join cultural activities together. He expressed his hope that through activities such as lantern processions, lion dances and mooncake tasting, Japanese children would learn more about Vietnamese culture, while Vietnamese children in Japan would have opportunities to experience and preserve traditional customs from their homeland. Despite the rain on the opening day, thousands of visitors came to explore and enjoy Vietnamese cuisine. Many stopped at food stalls to choose banh mi or hot dishes before continuing to discover other Vietnamese flavors. The organizers hoped the festival will become an annual event, providing a friendly venue for Japanese people to discover Vietnamese cuisine and for the Vietnamese community to share flavors from their homeland.

picked.t: Vietnam reaches highest tourism development ranking since Covid
picked.body: Vietnam scored 4.15 points out of 10 in the biennial ranking released on Friday by the World Economic Forum. The index measures the factors and policies that enable sustainable and resilient development of tourism like business environment, safety and health conditions, price competitiveness, air transport infrastructure, ground and port infrastructure, tourist services and infrastructure, natural resources, and cultural resources. In Southeast Asia, Vietnam ranked behind Singapore, which placed 13th globally, Indonesia at 23rd, Malaysia at 26th and Thailand at 38th. In terms of improvement, Vietnam's score rose 6.1 percentage points from 2024, outpacing regional revials such as Indonesia at 2.2 percentage points, Malaysia and Thailand at 5.8 each, and Singapore at 3.3. Vietnam performed well in price competitiveness, safety and security, air transport, port infrastructure, and natural resources. Thanks to political stability and a high level of safety, Vietnam has become a favorite destination for foreign tourists. The ranking reflects the World Economic Forum’s assessment of Vietnam’s stable, safe and secure socio-political environment amid global volatility and instability, according to the Vietnam National Authority of Tourism. Vietnam's air transport infrastructure also recorded major improvements. Tan Son Nhat International Airport in Ho Chi Minh City last year opened its VND11-trillion (US$430 million) domestic Terminal 3 , which is designed to serve up to 20 million passengers annually. The country is also getting Long Thanh International Airport in Dong Nai Province, next door to HCMC. During its first phase, slated for commercial operation later this year, the airport will have one runway, a passenger terminal and supporting infrastructure, and a capacity of 25 million passengers a year. It will replace Tan Son Nhat as Vietnam's largest aviation hub. Despite the gains, several areas remained relatively weak. Vietnam faces a number of challenges such as tourism infrastructure and services, prioritization of travel and tourism, and the socioeconomic impact of the sector. This provides a crucial foundation for Vietnam to strengthen its competitiveness, address existing gaps and pursue more sustainable, high-quality and effective tourism development, the tourism administration added. Japan reclaimed the top spot in this year's tourism development ranking. The U.S. ranked second, followed by Spain in third, Australia in fourth and France in fifth, according to the report.
